PASS for the full original P13.2 within the expressly permitted background. The new argument discharges QEP on each original normal rational quotient; it leaves no quotient-envelope or realization condition outstanding. The verified conclusion covers every normal good polarized affine cone in the stated setting, every dimension, every prescribed rational or irrational Reeb field, the original carrier K=X0^T, actual E1/R, and the genuine cone probability operator.

Background scope. The completion criteria expressly grant actual90’s complete QEP-conditional mathematical body, including its precise P13.1 and scoped73/79 inputs. They also grant actual91’s countable theorem and actual86’s countable-to-arbitrary implication, and expressly discharge E86. Their domains and polarizations match: EP_U concerns original reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective varieties and actual ample rational bundles over arbitrary algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero fields. Historical pending qualifications describe the earlier scopes; they do not revoke this express grant. Neither new94 nor the new quotient application was assumed proved. The granted backgrounds are excluded from the external-premise list and recorded separately in task passages.

Original quotient. Positivity on finitely many homogeneous algebra generators supplies positivity on every supported nonzero weight, since each such weight occurs in a monomial in those generators. The resulting open rational cone contains a rational vector. Clearing denominators and dividing the supported gcd supplies precisely the effective positive grading; it does not assume primitivity in an ineffective original lattice. The degree-d generator powers give a standard graded subalgebra over which R is finite, with the same irrelevant radical. Thus the original Proj is integral, projective, and has dimension n−1. Their covering charts trivialize the actual O(d); the finite-map construction proves ampleness. Further divisibility uses tensor powers of this same bundle. The corresponding Proj and finite-pullback criteria have the required hypotheses. [Stacks](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01Q2), [finite pullback](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XO).

Normality is proved on the original charts: an element of Frac((R_f)_0) integral over (R_f)_0 belongs to the normal localization R_f, and its grading invariance places it in degree zero. Localization then makes every local ring of Y a normal domain. The geometric-unibranch definition applies at every point, with identity residue-field extension. Consequently EP_U applies to Y itself and the actual ample rational O(d), over the original field of arbitrary cardinality. This supplies exactly actual90’s QEP witness. Reducedness over the perfect field also verifies geometric reducedness for the general-projective volume input. No smoothness hypothesis is inserted. [Normality and unibranchness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BQ3), [geometric reducedness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/020I).

Calibration. With p=n−1, the retained formulas are V_eta=s^(−n)d^(1−n)(L_d^p), omega=L_d/(sd), omega^p=sV_eta, chi=sd·u∘ell∘q, and E_eta=E_Ld/(sd). These factors are mutually consistent: the radial factor supplies the additional s^(−1), while the horizontal product has p factors (sd)^(−1). The projective probability divides by (L_d^p). The weighted correspondence consequently has the factor (sd)^(−1). Neither the carrier nor the probability convention changes.

Genuine unbounded correspondences. Splitting sections into eigencomponents retains the actual mL_d, coefficients, and global generation: simultaneous vanishing of all components would imply simultaneous vanishing of the original generating sections. The Gauss formula and ultrametric inequality give chi∘q≥chi, with the same reference. Uniform closure and raw decreasing defining nets extend this at every analytic point, including minus infinity. The fixed generic trivial valuation remains finite. Energy monotonicity therefore gives actual projective E1 membership. In the inverse direction, torifying a genuine defining net gives invariant continuous majorants; the calibrated continuous correspondence lifts them to a decreasing genuine cone net. Equivariance extends the limiting formula to every punctured-cone point. Retraction and the homeomorphism ell prove both inverses. Decreasing energy continuity preserves finite energy and also energy minus infinity. Simultaneous raw approximants, integrability of E1 tests, and weighted convergence establish both operator identities. The test-containing pairing minus the zero-test pairing has the correct sign. Closed support and mass one persist through the limits. [BJ, §§4 and 7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

Intrinsic dual criterion. The Radon decreasing-net integral argument is valid on compact Hausdorff K; compactness gives an entire tail below each continuous majorant plus epsilon. Thus it genuinely handles nets. Uniform FS approximation and decreasing energy/integral continuity identify the bounded-test and actual-E1 suprema. Finite dual energy gives integrability of every actual E1 potential. Conversely, the decreasing convex sums with weights 2^(−j), remaining reference weight, trivial-valuation value zero, and energy at least −1 produce an actual E1 contradiction if integration is unbounded on J≤1. The mixed expansion gives J(u_t)≤2^n t²J(u), and optimization gives the stated bound C+2^(n−2)C². This establishes the equivalence without assuming an inverse equation.

Midpoint estimate. The difference-of-powers telescope uses exactly j=0,…,p−1, so I=ΣB_j. The second derivative is −pΣ binom(p−1,j)t^j(1−t)^(p−1−j)B_j, with B_j≥0. The midpoint kernel is one half of min(t,1−t). On [1/4,3/4], its lower bound 1/8, interval length 1/2, and monomial bound 4^(−p+1) give exactly a_p=p/4^(p+1). Weighted decreasing approximation extends this inequality to actual E1. Nonnegativity of the midpoint deficit yields I(u,v)≤(d_u+d_v)/(2a_p), and the reference tangent deficit gives the asserted J bound. No completion argument is used here.

Actual compactness and target continuity. The supremum-test topology is Hausdorff by separation using genuine continuous defining majorants. The energy infimum gives upper semicontinuity in that topology. The map A is onto the normalized actual cone PSH space. Its global supremum identity is exact: invariance of the obstacle, q being a retraction, and chi∘q≥chi make the supremum on B equal the full projective supremum. BJ4.28 therefore makes A continuous, and BJ5.11 supplies compactness through this continuous surjection.

For the lifted target, torification on the same bundle is essential and is present: every projective E1 chi has invariant E1 chi∘q, and they agree on B. Its cone counterpart is target-integrable. Hence the lifted probability integrates every projective E1 potential, establishing the complete BJ9.20 antecedent. BJ9.19 then applies with divisorial convergence and bounded J on the integral projective Y. Its proof uses uniformly approximating model-measure pairings and outer differentiation, without an inverse equation or smoothness assumption. The corrected absolute-value identity proves absolute L1 convergence. The compact-subnet contradiction identifies Achi with the original cone limit and proves convergence of the entire original bounded-J net; it assumes no closedness of an invariant weak subset. [BJ, §§5 and 9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

Irrational transfer. The granted comparison inputs are used within their original cone scope. The positive generator ratios bound every finite orbit in both directions, preserve singular orbits, and give both uniform strict-gap implications needed for the root homeomorphisms. The stated J comparison supplies bounded energy for inverse roots. Each continuous orbit pushforward is a Radon probability and integrates every actual eta-E1 potential by the bounded orbit difference; the intrinsic criterion therefore makes it a finite-energy target. The root L1 proof fixes M and a finite rational grid before taking the original net limit, refines the mesh afterward, and sends M to infinity last. The positive-part tail estimate follows from source L1 convergence and its 1-Lipschitz scalar map. Null sets are needed only for finitely many functions at each index. This proves whole-net target L1 continuity at the prescribed irrational field. It transports potentials and topology; the operator identification remains at fixed xi.

Attainment and identification. A normalized actual FS maximizing sequence has bounded J. Compactness gives an actual normalized PSH subnet limit, energy upper semicontinuity makes it E1, and target L1 convergence makes its objective at least the supremum. The intrinsic dual equality supplies the opposite inequality. Thus an actual maximizer is attained. Continuous-majorant nets establish the outer-obstacle inequality for w+tf. The granted fixed-field outer derivative applies with both signs and the genuine probability operator. The direction lattice separates torified points, retains constants and lattice operations, and is uniformly dense. Positive and negative t force equality of target and genuine MA integrals on this lattice, hence on C(K). The projective relative-volume source retains its general geometrically reduced scope and exact normalization; its separate envelope-continuity assumption in §3.2 is not discarded. [BGM](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.03847v1).

Necessity and every maximizing sequence. The actual tangent inequality bounds the H dual supremum of an E1 output by E(u)−∫u MA(u), which is finite because the weighted E1 integrals are finite. Equality follows by testing u in the actual-E1 supremum. Support, positivity, and probability mass are those of the original operator. Bi-Lipschitzness on the image establishes uniqueness only after actual existence. For any normalized actual E1 maximizing sequence, the attained w has zero deficit, so the midpoint estimate gives I(u_j,w)≤d_j/(2a_p) for every j. For p=1, a_1=1/16 and the stated bound is 8d_j. The additional topology, target-L1, and energy convergence assertions follow from bounded J, compactness, identification of every cluster subnet, and the deficit identity.

Dimension one. The effective normal positive grading has degree-zero graded fraction field k and one-dimensional homogeneous pieces. Its supported semigroup has gcd one; normality saturates it inside the homogeneous fraction field, yielding N and R=k[z]. Torification and link normalization leave exactly the trivial valuation. The energy of the scalar potential is that scalar, the radial factor has unit mass, and the sole target probability has dual energy zero. Every normalized potential is zero. There is no use of a_0.

Harmless corrections and evidence boundary. Remove the duplicated comma in (8.2). In §7, ‘zero parameter’ refers to finite orbits; an identically minus-infinity orbit has the singular root value supplied by the granted decreasing-limit extension. These are wording clarifications, not substantive repairs. The supplied absolute-value, weighted-pairing, and ample-interpolation corrections are correct and retained. Short passage quotations below locate the opened primary statements; the hypotheses and pertinent proof bodies were checked, rather than treating those fragments, source headlines, hashes, historical verdicts, or compilation as proofs. This review does not certify the documentary build or byte-identity claims.

Final verified scope: the stated intrinsic necessary-and-sufficient image characterization, actual attainment, genuine fixed-xi equation, uniqueness modulo constants, and the exact every-maximizing-sequence I estimate hold throughout the full original P13.2 domain using the expressly granted backgrounds. No rational-only, smooth-quotient, countable-field, completion, or unresolved-realization restriction remains.

passages.statement: Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Example 3.9, Theorem 4.15(iii), and Corollary 4.16: on a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, for an actual ample rational line bundle L, Hdom(c1(L)) is contained in H(L) for that same bundle; every genuine PSH(c1(L)) potential has decreasing Hdom(c1(L)) majorants, and CPSH(c1(L)) is the uniform closure of Hdom(c1(L)).

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Example 3.9, Theorem 4.15(iii), and Corollary 4.16: on a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, for an actual ample rational line bundle L, Hdom(c1(L)) is contained in H(L) for that same bundle; every genuine PSH(c1(L)) potential has decreasing Hdom(c1(L)) majorants, and CPSH(c1(L)) is the uniform closure of Hdom(c1(L)).

Boucksom–Jonsson, Proposition 4.28: on a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, for a numerical class theta and each fixed continuous real obstacle gamma, phi↦sup(phi−gamma) is continuous on PSH(theta) in the topology of pointwise convergence on divisorial valuations.

Boucksom–Jonsson, Theorem 5.11: on an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, the envelope property for a numerical class theta is equivalent to compactness of the genuine normalized space {phi∈PSH(theta):sup phi=0} in the divisorial topology; the statement applies to arbitrary nets and field cardinality.

Boucksom–Jonsson, Theorem 7.1 and Proposition 7.7: on a reduced p-dimensional projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, ample-class energy pairings extend to genuine PSH tuples by the infimum over dominating Hdom potentials, are increasing and upper semicontinuous, and are continuous along decreasing nets. The normalized energy E_omega(phi)=(omega,phi)^(p+1)/((p+1)(omega^p)) is concave and satisfies E_omega(phi+c)=E_omega(phi)+c; E1 consists of actual PSH potentials with finite energy.

Boucksom–Jonsson, Theorem 7.18 and Propositions 7.19 and 7.21: on a reduced p-dimensional projective variety, p≥1, over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, ample E1 tuples define positive Radon mixed curvature measures with their mixed intersection mass. Every E1 test is integrable against these measures. Simultaneous decreasing PSH nets with E1 tuple limits give weak convergence of the mixed measures and of weighted measures whenever the limiting PSH weight is integrable against the limiting mixed measure.

Boucksom–Jonsson, Proposition 9.19: on a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field with an ample class omega, a divisorially convergent genuine PSH(omega) net whose J values are eventually bounded has an E1 limit and converges in L1(lambda) for every finite-dual-energy Radon probability lambda. No envelope property, smoothness, or inverse-equation existence hypothesis is required.

Boucksom–Jonsson, Theorem 9.20: on a reduced irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field with an ample class omega, a Radon probability lambda has finite dual energy sup_phi∈E1(omega)(E_omega(phi)−∫phi d lambda) if and only if every actual E1(omega) potential is lambda-integrable. The envelope property is not required.

passages.statement: Stacks Project, Definition 15.108.1: a local ring A is geometrically unibranch exactly when A_red is a domain, its integral closure in its fraction field is local, and the residue field of that integral closure is purely inseparable over the residue field of A.
passages.quote: the residue field of $A'$ is purely inseparable over the residue field of $A$.

passages.statement: Boucksom–Gubler–Martin, arXiv:2004.03847v1, Lemma 3.2: let Y be a geometrically reduced projective scheme of dimension p≥1 over a complete non-Archimedean field, L and M ample line bundles, phi a continuous psh metric on L, and psi_1,psi_2 continuous psh metrics on M. Set f=psi_1−psi_2 and C=((L+M)^p)−(L^p). With relative-volume normalization p!m^(−p−1), C inf f≤∫f(ddc phi+ddc psi_1)^p−vol(L,phi+f,phi)≤C sup f. This estimate has no envelope-continuity hypothesis; Section 3.2 separately imposes that hypothesis for its enveloped differentiability and orthogonality statements.

passages.statement: The one-parameter finite-continuous specialization of Boucksom–Jonsson, Lemma 4.6: on a compact space Q, let F be a family of finite continuous real functions stable under addition of constants. If each member of a decreasing outer net is itself a pointwise decreasing limit from F, its pointwise limit, allowed to take minus infinity, is a single decreasing-net limit from F. Minimum closure of F is unnecessary.

Boucksom–Jonsson, Lemma 5.17: on an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field with an ample class omega, the envelope property is equivalent to continuity of P_omega(f) for every continuous obstacle f; under that property these envelopes are genuine omega-psh potentials.

Boucksom–Jonsson, Theorem 5.20 and Corollary 5.21: on a smooth connected projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, every nef numerical class has the envelope property and its genuine normalized PSH space is compact.

Boucksom–Jonsson, Corollary 10.6: on an equidimensional reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field with an ample class omega, if u∈PSH(omega), v∈E1(omega), and u≤v almost everywhere for MA_omega(v), then u≤v everywhere. No envelope property or inverse-equation existence hypothesis is required.

Boucksom–Jonsson, Theorem 13.1, continuous-obstacle case: on a reduced irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, for an ample class omega having the envelope property and a continuous obstacle f, psi=P_omega(f) is continuous and genuinely omega-psh, and ∫(f−psi) MA_omega(psi)=0.

Boucksom–Eriksson, arXiv:1805.01016v3, Examples 7.12 and Theorem 7.14: on a projective scheme over a complete non-Archimedean field, including a trivially valued field, a psh metric defined by decreasing Fubini–Study approximation on an actual semiample rational line bundle is a decreasing limit of smooth semipositive metrics on that same bundle. For a continuous metric the convergence is uniform, and regularized Fubini–Study formulas permit arbitrary real finite weights.
passages.quote: Every psh metric φ on a semiample Q-line bundle L is psh-regularizable.

passages.statement: Boucksom–Eriksson, Proposition 8.3(iv), Theorem 8.4, and Proposition 8.5: on a projective scheme over a complete non-Archimedean field, smooth mixed Monge–Ampère measures including the analytic fundamental cycle commute with complete-field-extension pushforward. On fixed rational line bundles they extend uniquely to continuous psh-regularizable metrics, continuously for uniform metric convergence and weak measure convergence; the resulting measures are positive and have the mixed intersection mass.

Wu, arXiv:2406.13684v1, Definitions 2.9, 3.1, and 5.1: for a normal polarized affine cone over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field with torus T and Reeb vector xi, H(xi) consists of finite homogeneous maxima (lambda_i−v(f_i))/<xi,wt(f_i)> with real weights and common zero locus equal to the vertex; CPSH(xi) is its local uniform closure in continuous equivariant functions, and genuine PSH(xi) consists of nontrivial pointwise decreasing CPSH-net limits.
Stacks Project, Lemma 30.17.2: if R is Noetherian, X and Y are proper over R, f:Y→X is finite and surjective, and L is an invertible sheaf on X, then L is ample if and only if f*L is ample.
Stacks Project, Lemma 28.27.12: if S is a graded ring and j:X→Proj(S) is an open immersion with X quasi-compact, then j*O(d) is an invertible ample sheaf for some positive integer d.
Stacks Project, Lemma 33.6.3: a reduced scheme over a perfect field is geometrically reduced over that field.
